sections.title: Introduction
sections.html:
Introduction

A boilerplate is a reusable starter project. Instead of creating the same files again and again, you keep one clean starter folder and copy it whenever you want to build a new website.

This book shows the complete process for building a multipage website boilerplate with Home, About, Services, Products, Cart, Checkout, Booking, Contact, Login, Dashboard, and Admin pages.

The goal is not to memorize code. The goal is to understand what each file does, how the layout works, and how to reuse the project for many future websites.

sections.title: Chapter 1 - What You Are Building
sections.html:
Chapter 1 - What You Are Building

You are building a complete website starter template. It is simple enough for beginners but structured enough to become a business website, online store, booking site, affiliate site, portfolio, or local service website.

Figure 1. Beginner workflow for rebuilding the website project.

Main Features

Sticky navigation bar

Mobile hamburger menu

Dark mode with saved preference

Reusable hero and page-hero sections

Responsive grid cards

Product search

Cart saved in browser localStorage

Checkout starter form

Booking and contact forms

Demo login that redirects to dashboard

Admin starter form for adding products

sections.html:

sections.title: Chapter 3 - Project Folder Setup
sections.html:
Chapter 3 - Project Folder Setup

Start with one clean folder. The folder is the home of the website. Every page, stylesheet, script, and image goes inside it.

Figure 2. Recommended folder structure.

Create a new folder named sunday-website-boilerplate.

Open VS Code.

Click File, then Open Folder.

Select the sunday-website-boilerplate folder.

Create the files listed in Figure 2.

Create an assets folder for logos, images, icons, and videos.

Important beginner rule: file names must match exactly. If your link says products.html, the file must be named products.html, not product.html or Products.html.

sections.title: Chapter 4 - Layout and Page Map
sections.html:
Chapter 4 - Layout and Page Map

A complete website needs a clear map. The home page introduces the website. Other pages handle specific jobs such as services, products, booking, checkout, and admin.

Figure 3. Multipage website layout map.

Reusable Layout Pattern

Header: logo, navigation links, dark mode button, mobile menu button.

Main content: hero, page title, cards, forms, or products.

Footer: copyright and useful links.

Script link: connects the page to script.js.

sections.title: Chapter 5 - Building the Home Page
sections.html:
Chapter 5 - Building the Home Page

The home page is the front door of the website. It gives visitors a quick idea of what the site does and where to go next.

Create index.html.

Add the standard HTML document structure.

Link styles.css inside the head.

Add the header and navigation.

Add a hero section with a headline, short paragraph, and buttons.

Add feature cards explaining what the boilerplate includes.

Add the footer.

Link script.js before the closing body tag.

What the Main Home Page Sections Do

The header stays at the top because CSS uses position: sticky.

The logo links back to index.html.

The nav links connect to other pages.

The hero section creates the big first impression.

The card grid explains the website features.

The footer closes the page and gives the site a finished look.

sections.title: Chapter 6 - Building the Design System
sections.html:
Chapter 6 - Building the Design System

The design system lives in styles.css. This file controls how the entire website looks. A good CSS file lets you change the look of the whole site from one place.

Key CSS Classes

.header controls the sticky top navigation.

.logo styles the brand name.

.nav controls desktop and mobile navigation links.

.hero controls the large home page section.

.page-hero controls smaller title sections on inner pages.

.grid creates responsive cards.

.card styles boxes used across the site.

.form styles booking, contact, login, and checkout forms.

.dark changes the site into dark mode.

@media makes the layout work on phones.

The layout uses repeatable classes. This is why the same card style can work for services, products, dashboard boxes, and admin panels.

sections.title: Chapter 7 - Adding JavaScript Features
sections.html:
Chapter 7 - Adding JavaScript Features

The JavaScript file makes the site interactive. Without script.js, the site still displays, but buttons such as the mobile menu, dark mode, cart, and forms will not behave properly.

Main JavaScript Features

Mobile menu opens and closes with the menu button.

Dark mode is saved in localStorage so the browser remembers it.

Product search filters product cards.

Add to Cart stores selected products in localStorage.

Cart page reads the saved cart and calculates total.

Checkout form shows a success message and clears the cart.

Booking and contact forms show confirmation messages.

Login form saves a demo login flag and redirects to dashboard.html.

Admin form adds a product name and price to the admin list.

sections.title: Chapter 8 - Building Business Pages
sections.html:
Chapter 8 - Building Business Pages

Business pages make the website feel complete and trustworthy. These pages are About, Services, Booking, and Contact.

About Page

The About page explains who the business is, what it does, and why people should trust it. Replace the sample story with your real story.

Services Page

The Services page uses the same grid and card classes from the home page. This keeps the design consistent.

Booking Page

The Booking page collects name, email, date, time, and a message. This is a front-end demo. For a real business, connect the form to email, a database, Google Calendar, or a booking service.

Contact Page

The Contact page collects customer messages. For a live site, connect it to Formspree, Netlify Forms, EmailJS, Supabase, or your own backend.

sections.title: Chapter 9 - Building Shop and Checkout Pages
sections.html:
Chapter 9 - Building Shop and Checkout Pages

The product system is a beginner-friendly demo. It teaches the structure of an online store without requiring a payment processor yet.

Products Page

Each product card includes a name, price, and Add to Cart button. The data-name attribute helps the search feature find matching products.

Cart Page

The cart page reads products from localStorage. localStorage is browser storage. It is useful for demos and beginner projects, but a real store should use a database and secure checkout.

Checkout Page

The checkout page collects customer information. The Pay with Card button currently shows a starter confirmation. A real payment connection can be added later with Stripe Checkout.

sections.title: Chapter 10 - Login, Dashboard, and Admin Pages
sections.html:
Chapter 10 - Login, Dashboard, and Admin Pages

The login, dashboard, and admin pages are starter pages. They are not secure authentication yet. They are included so you can understand the structure before connecting real login later.

login.html contains the demo login form.

dashboard.html shows simple dashboard statistic cards.

admin.html shows a starter product entry form.

For a real login system, connect Supabase, Firebase, Auth0, Clerk, or your own backend. Never use browser-only localStorage as real security for private admin pages.

sections.title: Chapter 11 - Graphics and Branding
sections.html:
Chapter 11 - Graphics and Branding

Graphics make the website look professional. You can start with simple branding and improve it later.

Recommended Graphics

Logo: place inside assets/images/logo.png.

Hero background: use a clean image or gradient.

Product images: use same size for all product cards.

Favicon: small browser icon named favicon.ico or favicon.png.

Social sharing image: 1200 x 630 image for Facebook and link previews.

Beginner Graphic Rules

Use one main brand color.

Use the same font style across the site.

Avoid busy backgrounds behind small text.

Compress images before uploading.

Use descriptive file names such as hero-bg.jpg or product-dog-bed.jpg.

sections.title: Chapter 12 - Testing the Website
sections.html:
Chapter 12 - Testing the Website

Testing is where you find small mistakes before publishing the website.

Open index.html with Live Server.

Click every navigation link.

Resize the browser to test mobile view.

Click the hamburger menu on mobile width.

Click the dark mode button and refresh the page.

Search products on products.html.

Add products to cart, then open cart.html.

Clear the cart and test again.

Submit the booking, contact, and checkout forms.

Test login.html and confirm it redirects to dashboard.html.

Common Beginner Problems

Blank page: check that the file was saved and opened correctly.

CSS not working: confirm the link says href="styles.css" and the file name matches.

JavaScript not working: confirm script.js is linked before </body>.

Images not showing: confirm the image path and file extension.

Links broken: confirm the page file exists with the same spelling.

sections.title: Chapter 13 - Preparing for GitHub and Vercel
sections.html:
Chapter 13 - Preparing for GitHub and Vercel

After the site works locally, you can publish it online. GitHub stores the code. Vercel turns the code into a live website.

Create a GitHub account if you do not have one.

Create a new repository.

Open the project folder in VS Code.

Use Git to commit the files.

Push the project to GitHub.

Go to Vercel and choose New Project.

Import the GitHub repository.

Deploy the project.

Open the live Vercel URL and test every page again.

When you make future changes, save your files, commit the changes, push to GitHub, and Vercel will redeploy the website.

sections.title: Chapter 14 - Preparing This as an Amazon KDP Book
sections.html:
Chapter 14 - Preparing This as an Amazon KDP Book

To publish this guide on Amazon, prepare it as a clean manuscript. Amazon KDP accepts DOCX for ebooks and paperback interiors.

KDP Manuscript Checklist

Use a clear title page.

Include a copyright page.

Include a table of contents.

Use consistent chapter headings.

Use readable body text.

Keep code blocks simple and not too wide.

Use original screenshots or diagrams.

Create a separate cover file using Canva, Photoshop, or another design tool.

Preview the book in Kindle Previewer before publishing.

Suggested Amazon Book Details

script.js

const menuBtn = document.getElementById("menuBtn");

const navMenu = document.getElementById("navMenu");

const darkModeBtn = document.getElementById("darkModeBtn");

if (menuBtn && navMenu) {

menuBtn.addEventListener("click", () => { navMenu.classList.toggle("show"); });

}

if (darkModeBtn) {

darkModeBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {

document.body.classList.toggle("dark");

localStorage.setItem("theme", document.body.classList.contains("dark") ? "dark" : "light");

});

}

if (localStorage.getItem("theme") === "dark") { document.body.classList.add("dark"); }

function addToCart(name, price) {

let cart = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cart")) || [];

cart.push({ name: name, price: price });

localStorage.setItem("cart", JSON.stringify(cart));

alert(name + " added to cart!");

}

const searchInput = document.getElementById("searchInput");

const products = document.querySelectorAll(".product");

if (searchInput) {

searchInput.addEventListener("input", () => {

const searchValue = searchInput.value.toLowerCase();

products.forEach((product) => {

const productName = product.dataset.name.toLowerCase();

product.style.display = productName.includes(searchValue) ? "block" : "none";

});

});

}

const cartItems = document.getElementById("cartItems");

const cartTotal = document.getElementById("cartTotal");

function displayCart() {

if (!cartItems || !cartTotal) return;

const cart = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cart")) || [];

cartItems.innerHTML = "";

let total = 0;

cart.forEach((item) => {

const li = document.createElement("li");

li.textContent = item.name + " - $" + item.price;

cartItems.appendChild(li);

total += item.price;

});

cartTotal.textContent = "Total: $" + total;

}

displayCart();

function clearCart() { localStorage.removeItem("cart"); displayCart(); }

const checkoutForm = document.getElementById("checkoutForm");

const checkoutMessage = document.getElementById("checkoutMessage");

if (checkoutForm) {

checkoutForm.addEventListener("submit", (e) => {

e.preventDefault();

checkoutMessage.textContent = "Checkout submitted! Stripe payment connection comes next.";

localStorage.removeItem("cart");

checkoutForm.reset();

});

}

const bookingForm = document.getElementById("bookingForm");

const bookingMessage = document.getElementById("bookingMessage");

if (bookingForm) {

bookingForm.addEventListener("submit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); bookingMessage.textContent = "Booking request submitted successfully!"; bookingF

}

const contactForm = document.getElementById("contactForm");

const contactMessage = document.getElementById("contactMessage");

if (contactForm) {

contactForm.addEventListener("submit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); contactMessage.textContent = "Message sent successfully!"; contactForm.reset();

}

const loginForm = document.getElementById("loginForm");

if (loginForm) {

loginForm.addEventListener("submit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); localStorage.setItem("loggedIn", "true"); window.location.href = "dashboard.html";

}

const adminProductForm = document.getElementById("adminProductForm");

const adminProductList = document.getElementById("adminProductList");

if (adminProductForm) {

adminProductForm.addEventListener("submit", (e) => {

e.preventDefault();

const name = document.getElementById("adminProductName").value;

const price = document.getElementById("adminProductPrice").value;

const li = document.createElement("li");

li.textContent = name + " - $" + price;

adminProductList.appendChild(li);

adminProductForm.reset();

});

}

sections.title: Appendix B - Page Templates Checklist
sections.html:
Appendix B - Page Templates Checklist

Use this checklist when creating the rest of the pages. Each page should have the same base structure: doctype, html, head, body, header, main section, footer, and script link.

about.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Use the same header. Add a page-hero with About Us and a card with your story.

services.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Use service cards inside a grid: Web Design, E-commerce Setup, Booking Website.

products.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include searchInput, product cards with data-name, and Add to Cart buttons.

cart.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include cartItems, cartTotal, Clear Cart button, and Proceed to Checkout link.

checkout.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include customer name, email, address, city, state, ZIP, and Pay with Card button.

booking.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include name, email, date, time, message, and submit button.

contact.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include name, email, message, and send button.

login.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include loginEmail, loginPassword, and a login form that redirects to dashboard.html.

dashboard.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include dashboard cards for Orders, Messages, and Bookings.

admin.html

<!DOCTYPE html>... Include adminProductForm, adminProductName, adminProductPrice, and adminProductList.

sections.title: Final Thoughts
sections.html:
Final Thoughts

You now have a reusable website starter that you can copy for future projects. The most important skill is repetition: copy the boilerplate, rename the brand, replace the content, test every page, and deploy. Each time you do it, you will get faster and more confident.
